Enantioselective Dear omative Cyclization of Homotryptamines
with Allenamides into Indolo[2,3-b]quinolines
Soumen Biswas,
a
Hanbyul Kim,
a
Kiet Le Anh Cao,
a
and Seunghoon Shin
a,
*
a
Department of Chemistry , Research Institute for Natural Sciences and Center for New Directions in Or ganic Synthesis (CNOS),
Hanyang University , 222 W angsimni-ro, Seongdong-gu, Seoul, 04763 (Korea)
E-mail: sshin@hanyang.ac.kr
Manuscript received: January 18, 2020; Revised manuscript received: March 7, 2020;
V ersion of record online: March 30, 2020
Supporting information for this article is available on the WWW under https://doi.or g/10.1002/adsc.202000083
Abstract: W e have developed a catalytic asymmet-
ric dearomative cyclization of homotryptamine
derivatives, furnishing enantioenriched indolo[2,3-
b]quinoline scaff olds. The activation of allenamides
in the presence of chiral phosphoric acids triggered
the dearomative cyclization in up to 99% ee.
Keywords: dearomative cyclization; homotrypt-
amine; indolo[2,3-b]quinolines; chiral Brønsted acid
catalysis
Dearomatization of indoles through electrophilic acti-
vation has led to a range of powerful synthetic methods
for polycyclic indolyl compounds.
[1]
In particular , there
have been many elegant asymmetric dearomative
cyclizations of tryptamine derivatives, affor ding pyrro-
loindolines under metal-
[2]
or or ganocatalytic
conditions,
[3,4]
triggered by various electrophiles (Sche-
me 1A). Despite these remarkable developments on
pyrroloindolines, cyclization of homotryptamine deriv-
atives into indolo[2,3-b]quinolines have been much
less studied (Scheme 1B).
[5]
Considering a variety of
naturally occurring indole alkaloids share this core
(Scheme 1C),
[6]
a highly enantioselective access to this
scaff old is desired, but only a few methods are
available to date.
[7]
Inspired by the pioneering studies on the electro-
philic activation of allenamides in gold-
[8]
and Brønsted
acid-catalysis,
[9]
we initially posited that allenamides
[10]
would be good electrophilic sources triggering the
dearomative cyclization of tryptamines as in Sche-
me 1A. T o the best of our knowledge, only a single
example of asymmetric dearomative cyclization of
tryptamine derivatives with allenamides has been
reported, employing chiral gold complexes.
[8f]
Prompted by the lack of non-noble metal methods,
we initially set out to search for conditions effecti ng
the dearomative cyclization of tryptamine derivatives 1
with an oxazolidinone-derived allenamide 2 a
(Scheme 2), employing chiral phosphoric acids (CP As)
(Figure 1). Use of 4 Å MS in toluene gave consistently
higher yield and selectivity than other desiccants-
solvent combinations.
[1 1]
Among various chiral
phosphoric acids screened, (R)-P A2 with 9-phenan-
threnyl group at 3,3’-positions of the binol was
identified as the most selective catalyst. These opti-
mized conditions could be applied to various trypt-
amines, having substitution at C5-position (1 a–e),
aff ording the corresponding pyrroindolines 3 a–e in
good enantioselectivity , although 6-Cl-substituted 1 f
led to poor % ee.
However , a major problem with the cyclization of
tryptamines 1 was the poor yield for 3. T ypically , the
products were accompanied by unidentified byprod-
ucts. For example, with tryptamine 1 g (PG = p-Ns),
significant amount of di-substitution product 3 g’ (20%,
69% ee) formed, along with 3 g (49%, 70% ee). The
formation of 3 g’ is due to the nucleophilicity of N-
atom of the indoline 3, which consumes the iminium
ion formed from the allenamide 2.
[2e,3b,8d]
Unfortunately ,
simple change of the stoichiometry of 1 vs. 2 failed to
improve the yield of 3 or 3’.
Given this, we posited that the dearomative cycliza-
tion of homotryptamine derivatives would suffer less
this problem, due to the increased steric crowding
around the indolinyl N-atom, adjacent to the 5/6-fused
bridgehead. Thus we set out to screen chiral
phosphoric acid scaf folds (T able 1) and found (S)-P A6
(TCyP) as the best catalyst (entry 6), furnishing indolo
[2,3-b]quinoline 5 a in 77% ee at rt. Lowering the
temperature to 0 ° C further increased the enantio-
selectivity to 85% ee (entry 1 1). However , change of
N-protecting groups as in 6 and 8 (entries 13–14), as
well as employment of diff erent allenamides 2 b–e
[1 1]
in place of 2 a were larg ely unsuccessful, affor ding
lower yields and/or enantioselectivities. The product 9

having N-methoxycarbonyl (Moc) group, was obtained
as an acyclic adduct.
[1 1]
Based on these optimized conditions (entry 1 1,
T able 1), various indolo[2,3-b]quinolines could be
eff iciently synthesized via dearomative cyclization of
homotrypatmines 4 (T able 2). Synthesis of 5 a could be
conducted in 1 mmol scale with essentially identical %
ee and yield, confirming the practicality of the process.
Substitution at the indole core (R
1
) in 4 was well-
tolerated at various positions. For example, a wide
range of substituents with varying electron-demand
were accommodated at C5 (5 b–g). In addition,
substitutions at C4 (5 h–i) and at C7 (5 j) positions
were also satisfactory , but 6-Cl (5 k) and 6-Me (5 l)
derivatives were obtained with markedly lower enan-
tioselectivity . Interestingly , the reaction with 4 g gave
di-substituted 5 g’ exclusively , irrespective of the
stoichiometry of 4 g and 2 a. Substitution at the aniline
moiety (R
2
) was also well-tolerated. For example, both
electron-donating and withdrawing groups at C4 (5 k–
o) and C5 (5 p–r), as well as at C3 (5 s) and C6 (5 t)
were accommodated, affor ding good % ee and yields
of 5. The absolute configuration of the products was
assigned based on the X-ray crystallographic structure
of 5 r (Figure S1).
[12]
In terms of the mechanism, several factors seemed
to aff ect the enantio-determining step. A N-Me homo-
tryptamine derivative 4 w gave a significantly lower %
ee, suggesting that the indole N � H in 4 take part in the
Scheme 1. Enantioselective dearomative cyclizations for poly-
cyclic indolyl compounds.

hydrogen bonding organization of the transition state.
The enantioselectivity also depended on the N-protect-
ing groups for aniline (6 and 8), underscoring the
importance of hydrogen bonding of aniline N � H as
well. Based on this, we propose the stereochemical
model as follows (Figure 2). Dual activation of both
allenamides 2 and tryptamine 4 is achieved by the
hydrogen bonding or ganization depicted in Figure 2.
Basic site of the phosphate in (S)-TCyP activates
homotryptamines via dual hydrogen bonding with the
indole and the aniline in 4, whereas activation of
allenamides 2 by protonation at C2 would form the α,
β-unsaturated iminium ion, setting the stage for
conjugate addition by the indole moiety of 4 (ionic
model (a)). Alternatively , basic phosphate may form a
covalent adduct with the iminium to form allylphos-
phate aminal (covalent model (b)), followed by the
S
N
2’ attack of indole C3 carbon. In fact, Bandini and
coworkers revealed that such possibility was more
favourable than path (a), according to DFT computa-
tional study .
[13]
Finally , the indolo[2,3-b]quinoline 5 a could be
functionalized into alcohols 10 and 1 1 as in Scheme 3.
Protection of aminal nitrogen, followed by hydrolysis
aff orded unstable aldehyde, which was reduced in-situ
into 10 in excellent overall yields (84%) with no
racemization. Oxidative cleavage of enamide in 5 a,
followed by reduction furnished a homologous alcohol
1 1. In addition, a regioselective fluorination of
enamide unit,
[14]
followed by a reductive workup
aff orded 1,2-fluoroalcohol 12 as a diastereomeric
mixture.
In summary , we have developed an orga nocatalytic
route to enantio-enriched indolo[2,3-b]quinolines.

Lack of enantioselective cyclization of homotrypt-
amines were addressed by use of allenamides as
suitable electrophilic precursors. T o the best of our
knowledge, this protocol is the first general or gano-
catalytic asymmetric cyclization of homotryptamine
derivatives.
Experimental Section
T o a flame-dried test tube was added 4 Å molecular sieve
(20.0 mg), 3-(2λ
5
-propa-1,2-dien-1-yl)oxazolidin-2-one 2 a
(12.5 mg, 0.10 mmol), and N-(2-((1H-indol-3-yl)methyl)
phenyl)-4-methylbenzenesulfonamide 4 a (75.3 mg, 0.20 mmol)
in toluene (1.0 mL) and the mixture was kept stirred in an ice-
bath. (S)-TCyP (P A6, 5.0 mg, 0.005 mmol) was then added and
the mixture was stirred at 0 ° C. After completion of the reaction
(monitored by TLC), the mixture was directly loaded onto a
silica gel column and flash column chromatography (EtOAc:
Hex = 1:6 to 1:2) afforded 3-((E)-3-((5aS,10bS)-5-tosyl-
5,5a,6,1 1-tetrahydro-10bH-indolo[2,3-b]quinolin-10b-yl)prop-1-
en-1-yl)oxazolidin-2-one 5 a (34.1 mg, 68%) as a white solid
(mp = 158–160 ° C). The enantioselectivity was determined by
Chiralpak
®
AD � H column using IP A:nHex (30:70) as an eluent
(1 mL/min).
